title: Agent Behavior Reverse Engineering
content: Agent behavior reverse engineering asks what an agent has done, based on theactions it has taken. In its simplest form, the answer is an instruction or promptthat describes the task carried out by those actions. The usual direction is to givean agent a task and let it act; here, the direction is reversed, from actions back to atask. This paper argues that this problem deserves attention as a research direction.It also extends the idea to multi-agent systems, where the aim is to understandwhat each agent did and what they accomplished together. The main motivation issafety: understanding actual behavior can help determine whether an agent carriedout a harmful task. For hypothetical future agents with self-awareness, this abilitycould also help people understand the activities those agents choose for themselvesand their consequences. This paper explains the idea, gives simple examples, andoutlines ways to begin studying it.
